stem: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a single row of six seats, all facing north. Q sits exactly between P and R, with one of them on each side of Q. T sits exactly between S and U, with one of them on each side of T. P is not adjacent to S. R is not adjacent to U. P sits somewhere to the left of T. U does not sit at either end of the row. Who occupies seat 4, counting from the left end?

per_option_rationale.rationale: T sits in seat 5, not seat 4. Reading the row R, Q, P, U, T, S one seat too far to the right lands on T, an off-by-one slip in the seat count.
S occupies seat 6, the right end. Choosing S ignores that U-not-at-either-end and P-left-of-T force the S, T, U block to sit on the right with U inward at seat 4 and S at the far seat 6, not seat 4.

The block Q-between-P-and-R and the block T-between-S-and-U must tile the six seats as two adjacent triples. P-left-of-T puts the P,Q,R block on the left. P-not-adjacent-to-S and R-not-adjacent-to-U force the P,Q,R block to read R, Q, P so P meets the junction, and U-not-at-either-end forces the second block to read U, T, S. The row is R, Q, P, U, T, S, so seat 4 is U.

Q sits in seat 2. Picking Q comes from orienting the first block as P, Q, R from the left, the reverse of the order the not-adjacent clues force; the correct orientation is R, Q, P, which puts Q in seat 2 but the junction person P in seat 3, not Q in seat 4.

explanation: The two between-clues are rigid 3-person blocks, and six seats hold exactly the two blocks side by side. P-left-of-T puts the P,Q,R block on the left half (seats 1 to 3) and the S,T,U block on the right half (seats 4 to 6). Within each block only the orientation is free. P must not be adjacent to S and R must not be adjacent to U, so at the seat-3 to seat-4 junction the left block reads R, Q, P (P inward) and U-not-at-either-end forces the right block to read U, T, S (U inward at seat 4). The unique row is R, Q, P, U, T, S, and seat 4 from the left is U.

explanation_sections.punchline: U-not-at-either-end is the cracker: it forces the right block to read U, T, S with U at the inner seat 4, so seat 4 is U.
explanation_sections.approach: Treat each between-clue as a fixed triple and note that six seats fit exactly two triples side by side. Use P-left-of-T to fix which block sits left. Then orient each block: the not-adjacent clues decide what sits at the seat 3 to seat 4 junction, and the end-exclusion clue on U decides the right block's orientation. Build R, Q, P, U, T, S and verify P not beside S, R not beside U, P left of T, and U off the ends all hold, then read seat 4.
explanation_sections.lesson: Merge rigid blocks by first deciding their left-right order, then orienting each from the constraints acting at the seam where the blocks meet.
explanation_sections.timing: About 170 seconds. Fastest elimination is option (2) S: U cannot sit at an end, which pushes S to the far right seat 6, so S can never be the inner seat 4.
